story: S&P 500 fell 11.6% from its Oct 6 record to a Nov 20 close (correction), rebounded 5.6% to 7,297.49 by Nov 27; why a fall needs a bigger gain to recover

scenes.hook: The S&P 500 fell [[11.6%,]] then bounced 5.6% in one week.
scenes.say: The S and P five hundred fell eleven point six percent, then bounced five point six percent in one week. In the next minute, you'll learn what that means, and why recoveries are harder than they look.

scenes.note: Source: AP, S&P Dow Jones Indices closes. Correction = 10% below a record.
scenes.say: A correction is a drop of ten percent or more from a recent high. The index closed at a record, seven thousand eight hundred nineteen, on October sixth. On November twentieth it closed at six thousand nine hundred ten. That is eleven point six percent lower.

scenes.note: Illustrative: simple percentage math on $100. Computed from the closes above.
scenes.say: Here's the catch. Lose eleven point six percent, and you need a gain of thirteen point one percent to get back. Take one hundred dollars. After the fall it is eighty-eight dollars forty. That smaller amount has to grow more.

scenes.note: Sources: AP, Nov 27 close. Analysts point to a bounce in battered AI stocks.

elements.text: Up 5.6% since the Nov 20 close. Analysts point to a bounce in battered AI stocks.

scenes.say: Then came a rebound. On Friday, the index closed at seven thousand two hundred ninety-seven. That is five point six percent above its November twentieth close. Analysts point to a bounce in battered A I stocks.

scenes.note: Computed from AP closes: 7,297.49 vs the 7,818.93 record of Oct 6.
scenes.say: Even after the bounce, the index is still six point seven percent below its record. It needs about seven point one percent more to get there. A fall of ten to twenty percent is a correction. Beyond that, a bear market.

elements.text: Percentages are not symmetric: the deeper the fall, the bigger the gain needed to recover.

scenes.say: The takeaway: percentages are not symmetric. The deeper the fall, the bigger the climb back. Follow Market Ledger for one explainer a day.
